correctness.rationale: The Kesten adjacency Plancherel density and unique radial Bochner representation imply that signed positivity is equivalent to nonnegativity of one explicit measure. Exact resolvent identities give F_u for every radius, with a positive complementary atom beyond q^(-1/2). The unmatched atom yields the s>critical obstruction; unbounded edge density yields the s=critical obstruction. For subcritical s the derivative of F_r/F_s has the verified sign of 1-qrs, giving the exact endpoint minimum. At qrs=1 the continuous part vanishes and the remaining atom is C_r delta_{r^(-1)+qr}. The finite-site strictness argument integrates nonnegative spherical forms against positive continuous density. The embedded program passed exact symbolic and finite supplementary checks.

value.rationale: The sharp subtractive covariance feasibility cone is a natural quantitative spectral-design problem on homogeneous trees. The answer is a complete degree/scale classification with a true no-go region, an obstruction switching between two Kesten spectral edges, and a nontrivial pure complementary spherical covariance at resonance. It isolates a mathematically useful phase transition not supplied by general positivity of each exponential alone.
